newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends weak as Cetes at post-crisis lows.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends weak as Cetes at post-crisis lows.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed down across the board on Wednesday after dealers covered dollar positions following a fall in primary Cetes (Treasury Certificates) rates to their lowest levels since the December 1994 devaluation crisis, traders said.
"Foreign investors began to cover (dollar) positions from early on, followed by local banks and corporations that still needed to cover month-end obligations," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 2.7 and 2.8 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.8400/7.8450 and 7.8360/7.8410 per dollar.

Banco de Mexico assigned bellwether 28-day Cetes at 21.91 percent at Tuesday night's primary auction, a fall of 102 basis points from last week's rate. This came as a surprise to dealers, who had been expecting a fall of no more than 53 basis points on average, according to a Reuters survey.
Traders noted, however, that the 48-hour peso did respect support at 7.85 per dollar.
"The peso settled in line with the new primary interest rates, but support held up at 7.85 pesos (per dollar) when U.S. long bond yields receded slightly," another trader said.
Yields on U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds declined to 6.91 percent on Wednesday, down from 6.93 percent on Tuesday.
Same-day peso contracts had closed earlier 2.6 centavos weaker at 7.8320/7.8360 per dollar.
